  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */

      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="580mm" height="87.7mm" viewBox="0 0 580 87.7" data-device="s9311-64d" data-view="left" data-switching-capacity="25.6 Tbps" data-packet-throughput="10.6 Bpps" data-power-typical-w="387.5" data-power-max-w="2097" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="200 to 240 V, 16 A" data-input-dc="-48 to -60 V, 70 A" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 hot-swappable" data-fan-redundancy="3+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Tomahawk 4" data-cpu="Intel Icelake-D 4-core @ 2.4 GHz" data-memory="2x 16 GB DDR4 R-DIMM with ECC" data-storage="1x 128 GB SSD" data-bmc="Aspeed AST2620" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list)" data-optics-sfp-plus="1/10G (datasheet port list)" data-zr-capacity="up to 32 QSFP-DD ZR+ modules; the HIG's Figure 12 shades one 32-port band to mark which ports they are - see the zr-port-set gap" data-timing-cable="SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector, for 1PPS and 10MHz" data-timing="1PPS and 10MHz SMB (Premium), each input/output" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; BSMI (CNS 13438), Class A; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='ufispace/fan-805616@'] .state-fault { --led-color: #eab308; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/fan-805616@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-242-dc@'] .state-critical { --led-color: #eab308; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-242-dc@'] .state-ok { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-242-dc@'] .state-standby { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-242-dc@'] .state-standby { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-242-dc@'] .state-warning { --led-color: #eab308; }
    g[data-ref^='ufispace/psu-242-dc@'] .state-warning { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="580mm" height="87.7mm" viewBox="0 0 580 87.7" data-device="s9311-64d" data-view="right" data-switching-capacity="25.6 Tbps" data-packet-throughput="10.6 Bpps" data-power-typical-w="387.5" data-power-max-w="2097" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="200 to 240 V, 16 A" data-input-dc="-48 to -60 V, 70 A" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 hot-swappable" data-fan-redundancy="3+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Tomahawk 4" data-cpu="Intel Icelake-D 4-core @ 2.4 GHz" data-memory="2x 16 GB DDR4 R-DIMM with ECC" data-storage="1x 128 GB SSD" data-bmc="Aspeed AST2620" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list)" data-optics-sfp-plus="1/10G (datasheet port list)" data-zr-capacity="up to 32 QSFP-DD ZR+ modules; the HIG's Figure 12 shades one 32-port band to mark which ports they are - see the zr-port-set gap" data-timing-cable="SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector, for 1PPS and 10MHz" data-timing="1PPS and 10MHz SMB (Premium), each input/output" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; BSMI (CNS 13438), Class A; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="436mm" height="580mm" viewBox="0 0 436 580" data-device="s9311-64d" data-view="top" data-switching-capacity="25.6 Tbps" data-packet-throughput="10.6 Bpps" data-power-typical-w="387.5" data-power-max-w="2097" data-power-envelope="bare" data-input-ac="200 to 240 V, 16 A" data-input-dc="-48 to -60 V, 70 A" data-psu-redundancy="1+1 hot-swappable" data-fan-redundancy="3+1 hot-swappable" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C" data-operating-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C" data-storage-humidity="5 to 95% RH non-condensing" data-asic="Broadcom Tomahawk 4" data-cpu="Intel Icelake-D 4-core @ 2.4 GHz" data-memory="2x 16 GB DDR4 R-DIMM with ECC" data-storage="1x 128 GB SSD" data-bmc="Aspeed AST2620" data-optics-qsfp-dd="400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list)" data-optics-sfp-plus="1/10G (datasheet port list)" data-zr-capacity="up to 32 QSFP-DD ZR+ modules; the HIG's Figure 12 shades one 32-port band to mark which ports they are - see the zr-port-set gap" data-timing-cable="SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector, for 1PPS and 10MHz" data-timing="1PPS and 10MHz SMB (Premium), each input/output" data-console="RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console" data-oob="1x RJ45 100/1000M" data-safety="UL 62368-1; IEC 62368-1" data-emc="FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; BSMI (CNS 13438), Class A; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A" data-environment="RoHS; WEEE" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
